data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test constrains its subject when the test is a guard-installation certificate: the test passes only if a specific guard exists, and the guard exists only because the test was shown failing against a planted mutation. The 3-of-26 survivors are the three mutations where the guard checks declared data but the mutation adds behavior \u2014 a category the shown-to-fail ritual cannot see because the failing test was authored against declared structure, not added behavior.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the 3 surviving mutations are shown to change declared data and still survive, the declared-vs-added distinction does not hold.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If compile.py's lost mutation is in a purely syntactic transformation with no behavioral addition, the added-behavior mechanism fails.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If an ordinarily-guarded module at 6/7 catches a behavior-adding mutation that shown-to-fail modules miss, the installation mode is not the differentiator.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the guard in question is demonstrated to check behavior via execution traces rather than declared data, the declared-data limitation is false.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The shown-to-fail-first installation creates a binding between test and guard that is asymmetric: the test can only constrain what it can name. When the planted mutation changes declared data, the test fails on the declared-data check and the guard is installed to check declared data. When a different mutation adds behavior without changing declared data, the guard passes silently \u2014 it constrains the declared subject but does not describe the added behavior. The 3 survivors are one bug in two costumes: a guard that checks declared data does not see added behavior. The 1-of-9 compile.py loss is the same asymmetry at compiler scale: the mutation lost under shown-to-fail-first was one that added behavior to a code path the guard's declared-data check could not reach.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
